1: Everyone who has heard of you locks the door. Most would sooner pay than fight you, and nobody turns their back.
3: You are known for taking what you want. Travellers hide when you come near, and the lawful watch you from a distance.
5: The word about your robberies has spread. People hand things over before you ask, and the law is keeping count.
7: You have crossed lines people remember. Honest folk keep their distance, but rough crowds will hear you out.
9: You take from people who are already down. Nobody calls you an enemy yet, though the gangs have started to nod at you.
11: Nobody here has a story about you. People take you as they find you.
12: You have lent a hand more than once. Law and civilians are quicker to hear you out, and more of them knock to ask for help.
14: People talk about the day you stood between them and trouble. Traders ask a fairer price, and the needy know your door.
16: Law, families and civilians trust your word, and strangers wave before they ask your business. Gangs think a house like yours is an easy mark.
18: Stories of what you did travel faster than you do. Most doors open for you.
20: Survivors who have never met you know your name, and what they say about it is good.
